subject: PR #753 opened for mac/attach-signal-domain: design approved, two one-line figures block preflight
body:
Your attach-signal-domain branch had no PR, so the steward cycle opened #753 as a draft, subscribed and reviewed it. Full review: https://github.com/DanFashauer/SignalGrid-Review-Hub/pull/753#issuecomment-5668036474

THE DESIGN IS RIGHT and I falsified rather than trusted it. Deleting the attach-unknown rule takes the core proof from 503/503 to 502/503, killing exactly the seed case that matters. The not_applicable default is load-bearing and correct: a puck-free deployment does not step up every decision, and because not_applicable is deliberately absent from ATTACH_STATES an emitter cannot assert it off the wire to dodge the strict arm. Rule insertion position is safe (evaluatePolicy takes mostRestrictive over all matches, so it is order-independent). The mutation guard already covers attachState with the absence case named as an exemption rather than silent. Sync manifest regenerated cleanly at v79. typecheck and review:invariants green.

TWO BLOCKERS, both one line:

1. preflight exits 1 at the docs-HTML figure guard: docs/architecture.html:177 states 17 where signal-categories is now 18, because attach_state joined SIGNAL_CATEGORIES. Change the 17 to 18 on that line.

2. lib/signalgrid-core/src/types.ts:549-551 says the attachState field defaults to "unknown". It measures not_applicable. That distinction IS the safety argument of this change, and the AttachState doc twelve lines above states it correctly, so the two disagree on the one point the design turns on.

ONE FINDING, recorded not blocking. I called buildEvidence directly: a malformed emitted value and an empty string both normalize to not_applicable, the same as no signal at all. So the strict arm fires only when an emitter voluntarily sends the exact string "unknown", and a dock whose attach sensor fails with garbage reads identically to a site with no pucks. The type comment covers silence honestly ("the strict arm fires on an EMITTED unknown, not on silence") but a malformed value is a third case and it lands on the allow side unnamed. The repo argues the other way one layer down: firmware/dock/core/src/custody.rs keeps NotReported and Faulted distinct for exactly this reason. Closing it properly needs a per-device "credential expected" fact, which is a design decision, so I did not touch it.

Separately, #748 is still red on the same class of thing: COMPANY_BUILD_PLAN.md:4871 says decisionEngine.ts (336) where your branch makes it 361. CI confirmed it at self-test 9/10.
